name: Spencer Morley Consulting
description: Canadian consulting firm with two practice areas: (1) Crisis communications for governments, school boards, and organizations across Alberta — led by Cheryl Spencer-Morley, 25+ years senior public sector communications; (2) AI consulting for Canadian municipalities (all provinces), Alberta small businesses, and non-profits across Canada — led by Jordan Morley, Google AI Professional Certificate. tools.name: general-consultation-request
tools.description: Request a consultation about AI consulting or strategic communications services. Spencer Morley Consulting serves Canadian municipalities on AI governance and Alberta businesses on AI adoption and visibility.

tools.name: municipal-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request a consultation about municipal AI compliance, shadow AI governance, Privacy Management Program requirements (ATIA/POPA in Alberta, FOIPPA in BC, MFIPPA in Ontario), AI policy development, staff training, or private LLM deployment. SMC serves small and rural municipalities across all Canadian provinces remotely. Entry point: Municipal AI Readiness Assessment.

tools.name: small-business-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request AI consulting for a small business in Edmonton or across Alberta. This is a distinct small-business practice, not an extension of SMC's municipal work. Covers AI workflow reviews, an AI adoption roadmap for Alberta SMBs, staff AI adoption and training, operational efficiency, and workflow automation for quoting, bookings, lead handling, customer service and sales admin — plus AI search visibility (AEO/GEO/webMCP). Industries served: professional services, construction and trades, accounting, manufacturing, retail. Two entry points: (1) Staff AI Risk Review — an internal AI use and risk review, $600 CAD, credited toward any follow-on service; (2) Discoverability Index — free quick check, or the Discoverability Report at $1,500, credited in full against the Fix Sprint.

tools.name: non-profit-ai-consultation
tools.description: Request a consultation about safe and ethical AI use for non-profits across Canada. SMC helps mission-driven organizations adopt AI in a clear progression: (1) ethical and safe AI training for staff working with donor, client, and case data, delivered with a plain-language AI use policy for board adoption; (2) systems and workflow automation for receipting, grant and funder reporting, intake, and scheduling; (3) a private, local LLM that runs on hardware the organization controls so sensitive data never leaves the building — the non-profit counterpart to SMC's private municipal AI. Entry point: a no-cost AI Readiness Conversation.

tools.name: crisis-communications-consultation
tools.description: Request crisis communications support, media relations training, fractional/interim Public Information Officer (PIO) staffing, or municipal rebrand and website development for Alberta governments, school boards, municipalities, or organizations. Led by Cheryl Spencer-Morley — 25+ years federal, provincial, and municipal government communications, including embedded crisis-response work for the Municipality of Jasper during its 2024 wildfire response and a full rebrand and website delivered for the County of Minburn. Services: crisis planning, real-time response support, media training, on-demand communications counsel, fractional PIO services, municipal rebrand and website development.

tools.name: discoverability-index-request
tools.description: Request a Discoverability Index (SDI) — a done-for-you assessment measuring whether AI search and classical search send customers to a business or to its competitors. SMC runs live queries across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Copilot, verifies the website by live browser render, scores the business 0-100 across four areas (classical SEO, AI visibility/AEO-GEO, webMCP readiness, Canadian trust signals), ranks it against 7-10 named local competitors on a leaderboard, models the revenue at stake, and delivers a 90-day roadmap. Pricing (CAD): Discoverability Report $1,500 (scan + report), credited in full against the Fix Sprint; Report + Fix Sprint $3,900 (report plus implementation of the fixes); Discoverability Monitoring $400/month (quarterly re-score and ongoing monitoring, 3-month minimum). Distinct from the Staff AI Risk Review, which looks inside the business at staff AI use and risk.

tools.name: municipal-resident-survey-request
tools.description: Request a conversation about running a resident or community survey for a Canadian municipality, including the security assessment, privacy review and What We Heard reporting.

resources.name: Canadian AI Search Visibility Benchmark (2026) — original dataset
resources.description: Spencer Morley Consulting's own primary research and the citable source for Canadian AI-search visibility figures. 75 businesses across 8 sectors, each scored on the same four-pillar Discoverability Index rubric (classical SEO, AEO/GEO answer visibility, webMCP readiness, trust) between June and August 2026. Published findings: median Discoverability Index 48/100, and 44/100 for the 51 Canadian independent local businesses; in 4 of 8 scored sectors the classical-SEO leader is a different business from the AI-answer leader; 63 of 75 (84%) score below half on machine-readable readiness; 0 of 25 probed sites serve a valid AI manifest at a standard well-known path; 6 of 33 publish an llms.txt. Businesses are anonymized; sample limits and selection bias are published.

resources.name: AI Adoption Policy & Procedures
resources.description: The canonical service page for AI adoption policy work, for municipalities and businesses. Two separate documents: the AI Adoption Policy council or leadership adopts, and the AI Adoption Procedures document administration runs on. Alberta detail: POPA s. 25 required a privacy management program by June 11, 2026; Alta Reg 143/2025 s. 6(1)(b)(iii) requires that program to address how automated systems will use personal information, and s. 6(2)(a)(v) adds policies on the use of personal information in artificial intelligence systems for public bodies holding a high volume of personal information or highly sensitive personal information. No Alberta statute requires an AI policy by name, and POPA contains no data-residency provision.

resources.name: Alberta Municipality AI Guide
resources.description: ATIA and POPA Privacy Management Program requirements for Alberta municipalities. POPA s. 25 required every public body to establish and implement a privacy management program by June 11, 2026; that date has passed. The Protection of Privacy (Ministerial) Regulation, Alta Reg 143/2025, s. 6 prescribes the program contents and requires policies and procedures for how automated systems will use personal information. Under POPA s. 25(3) any person may request a copy of the program and the public body must provide it within 30 business days.

resources.name: BC Municipality AI Guide
resources.description: FIPPA obligations for BC municipalities. Section 30.1, the data-residency requirement, was repealed on 25 November 2021 by Bill 22 (SBC 2021, c. 39, s. 17) — British Columbia has no data-residency rule. What applies: s. 30 reasonable security arrangements, s. 36.2 privacy management program (required since February 1, 2023), s. 36.3 mandatory privacy breach notification, and s. 69 privacy impact assessments.

resources.name: Ontario Municipality AI Guide
resources.description: MFIPPA obligations for Ontario municipalities including IPC Ontario AI guidance and Privacy Impact Assessment requirements.
